candidate.category_rationale: Correctness is decided by regional seismic network practice for local magnitude (Wood-Anderson record amplitude, -log A0 distance correction, station terms, reading selection, robust network aggregation), which is observational seismology. Closest rejected pair: Science / Physics (wave attenuation physics is background, but the graded object is a network's magnitude reduction procedure, not a physical model); Software / Data engineering rejected because the deliverable's correctness is domain arithmetic, not pipeline plumbing.

candidate.objective_type: seeded-departure repair of a seismic network local-magnitude reduction package against its numbered in-environment processing manual

domain_crux.failure_mode: a regional network's ML reduction drifts from its own processing manual in the ways real networks drift from Richter memory (nominal 2800 Wood-Anderson gain, peak-to-peak not halved, epicentral distance, log-distance interpolation, largest-channel station value, station term sign, mean network value, no minimum station count)
domain_crux.native_work_surface: small Python bulletin-reduction package plus the network's numbered manual part NPM-4 with its own -log A0 table
domain_crux.native_artifact_or_behavior: per-event report of station magnitudes, hypocentral distances, contributor flags and network ML
domain_crux.difficulty_without_incidental_convention: with every exact convention stated in NPM-4, the solver must still (a) apply the reading definition inside the station mean it has to rebuild (the shipped largest-channel code never needed it because a sub-noise amplitude rarely wins a max and the rule never applied), and (b) stop the new linear-in-distance interpolation at the table's ends, keeping the shipped log-distance extrapolation for stations the table does not reach; both are scope judgements a self-built reference from the manual does not settle for them

pattern_blind_crux_card.natural_domain_failure_mode: an analyst modernises a magnitude routine from the manual and either averages every trace the picker produced (noise-swamped strong-motion channels included) or extends the corrected interpolation past the calibrated table
pattern_blind_crux_card.native_work_surface_and_artifact: bulletin package + NPM-4 manual -> JSON magnitude report per event
pattern_blind_crux_card.why_difficulty_survives_removing_inciden: both traps live in domain definitions (what a reading is; how far the calibration reaches) inside aggregates the departures force the solver to rewrite, not in field names or ordering
two_natural_but_wrong_repairs_on_distinc: station.py: station_magnitude rebuilt as the mean over every amplitude of the recording (reading definition 2.3 not applied inside the new mean)

attenuation.py: minus_log_a0 converted from log-distance to linear-in-distance for every distance, so stations nearer than 10 km or farther than 600 km get a linearly extrapolated (or clamped) correction instead of the shipped log-distance extrapolation
pattern_blind_crux_card.direct_observable: report.events[].stations[].ml for the station carrying the trap input; everything else in the report unchanged

scope_ledger.primary_outcome: the bulletin report (station ML, hypocentral distance, contributor flag, network ML per event) that NPM-4 defines, printed by the frozen driver
scope_ledger.causal_core: picker amplitude -> record amplitude (gain, half p2p) -> readings (2.3) -> channel magnitude (+ -log A0 at hypocentral distance, + station correction) -> station mean -> contributors by table reach -> median with a three-station minimum

core_obligations.plausible_wrong: use the picker's peak-to-peak value as the record amplitude

TRAP T2: the correction for a distance the table does not reach keeps the shipped log-distance end-segment extrapolation, fed with the hypocentral distance
core_obligations.authority: instruction silence clause + NPM-4 3.2 'The table runs from 10 km to 600 km' + 3.3 'Between two listed distances'
core_obligations.plausible_wrong: linear-in-distance extrapolation of the end segments, or clamping to the end values

core_obligations.contribution: station ML is the mean of its readings' channel magnitudes
TRAP T1: only amplitudes at least three times their channel noise enter the station mean
core_obligations.plausible_wrong: average every amplitude of the recording

T1_READINGS.kind: exclusion via a definition hop inside an aggregate a departure forces the solver to rebuild
T1_READINGS.site: mlnet/station.py station_magnitude (rebuilt for departure 4.3 max -> mean)
T1_READINGS.subtype: an amplitude whose amplitude_nm is below 3 x noise_nm, in the same homogeneous `amplitudes` list; bare values, no label; excluded only by the domain-word definition 2.3 'A reading is an amplitude at least three times the noise of its channel'
T1_READINGS.hops: list field is `amplitudes` -> rule 4.3 speaks of readings -> definition 2.3 decides membership from two bare numbers
T1_READINGS.why_shipped_hides_it: shipped takes max(amplitude_nm); a sub-noise amplitude only changes a max when it is the largest, so the shipped code carries no filter and the solver's rebuilt mean inherits none
T1_READINGS.correct_fix: filter amplitudes by amplitude_nm >= 3*noise_nm before forming channel magnitudes and their mean
T1_READINGS.natural_wrong_repair: mean over every amplitude of the recording
T1_READINGS.isolated_test: test_station_mean_leaves_out_amplitudes_under_three_times_noise (only test whose inputs carry a sub-noise amplitude; includes an exact 3x integer boundary where product and ratio forms agree)

screen_4_3.competing_positive_enumeration: none: no sentence says every amplitude gives a channel magnitude; 4.1 says 'Each reading gives a channel magnitude'; 2.1 describes measurement only
screen_4_3.definitional_chain: yes: 2.3 defines reading; 4.1 and 4.3 speak only of readings
screen_4_3.contrary_expert_instinct: none: seismologists routinely drop low-SNR amplitudes; instinct agrees with the definition
screen_4_3.unnamed_shared_step: none: the line is drawn by the defined term 'reading'
screen_4_3.trap_in_several_tests: no: sweeps, generated and limits fixtures carry only amplitudes >= 4x noise

T1_READINGS.status_after_contract_review: demoted to a departure (CR-3: the blind reviewer read rule 2.3 as a plainly stated departure); kept in its own isolated test, not counted as a trap

T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.kind: 'apply the formula everywhere' edge in a function already being edited, with the book bounding the rule's range
T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.site: mlnet/attenuation.py minus_log_a0 (rewritten for departure 3.3 log-distance -> linear-in-distance)
T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.subtype: hypocentral distance below 10 km or above 600 km; section 1 admits 1 to ~1001.8 km
T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.why_silent: 3.2 gives values 10-600 km and says 'The table runs from 10 km to 600 km'; 3.3 governs only 'Between two listed distances'; 4.1 needs 'the distance correction at the station's distance', a value the manual does not define there -> instruction value-level silence: keep the code's calculation fed with manual-defined quantities (hypocentral distance)
T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.correct_fix: linear in distance inside [10, 600]; outside keep the shipped end-segment log-distance extrapolation, evaluated at the hypocentral distance
T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.natural_wrong_repair: swap log10(d) for d in the shipped segment formula (linear extrapolation beyond the ends), or clamp to the end values
T2_OFF_TABLE_KEPT.isolated_test: test_station_beyond_the_table_keeps_the_shipped_correction (only test with an off-table station; its event keeps >= 3 in-table contributors so the network value is unaffected by the trap)

screen_4_3.competing_positive_enumeration: checked: 3.3 is bounded by 'Between two listed distances'; 4.1 references the correction without defining it; 6.1 requires an ml for every station, which the kept calculation supplies; no sentence supplies an off-table value
screen_4_3.definitional_chain: yes: 3.2 table reach + 5.1 contributor reach (same bounds) + 3.3 bounded domain + instruction silence clause
screen_4_3.contrary_expert_instinct: mild: some analysts would null or clamp an uncalibrated station value; the silence clause forbids adding exclusions or clamps; extrapolation itself is the common practice so keeping one is not counter-intuitive
screen_4_3.unnamed_shared_step: the interpolation step is shared, but the governed/silent line is drawn by the defined bounds (listed distances, 10 to 600 km)
screen_4_3.trap_in_several_tests: no: every other fixture keeps hypocentral distances within [10, 600]

restraint_traps.independence: T2 (attenuation.py, distance correction, apply-everywhere edge, silent) and T3 (bulletin.py/station.py, recordings list, definition-hop grouping, governed) differ in file, list, subtype, manual section and instruction phrase

T3_STATION_GROUPING.kind: bare-value two-hop grouping/inclusion decision inside the aggregates departures 4.3 (station mean) and 5.2/5.3 (median, three-station minimum) force the solver to rebuild
T3_STATION_GROUPING.subtype: a station code that appears in two recordings of one event (broadband and strong-motion sensors processed separately, same epi_km, distinct channels); nothing labels it, it is a repeated code in the homogeneous `recordings` list
T3_STATION_GROUPING.hops: 1.2 defines a recording as one sensor's share of an event at a station -> 4.3 a station's magnitude is the mean of ITS readings (all its recordings) -> 5.2/5.3 speak of contributing stations, so the station votes once
T3_STATION_GROUPING.why_shipped_hides_it: the shipped loop computes one magnitude per recording and averages rows; the generated/sample data never repeat a code, so a self-built reference written per recording agrees with the natural rebuild
T3_STATION_GROUPING.correct_fix: pool amplitudes by station code within the event, one station magnitude reported on each of its recordings, median and count over stations
natural_wrong_repairs: per-recording station magnitude and per-recording counting (shipped structure kept)
readings pooled but median/count taken over recordings (double vote)
T3_STATION_GROUPING.isolated_test: test_two_sensors_of_one_site_are_one_station (only family with a repeated station; includes a two-station/three-recording event that must stay null and 1+2-reading splits where pooled mean != mean of means)

screen_4_3.definitional_chain: yes: 1.2 recording definition, 4.3 station's readings, 5.2/5.3 stations
screen_4_3.contrary_expert_instinct: none: one station one vote and pooling co-located sensors agree with practice
screen_4_3.unnamed_shared_step: none: line drawn by the defined terms station vs recording

solver_path_screen.premortem: A strong solver reads NPM-4, writes a ~60-line reference (half p2p x 2080e-6, hypot, linear interp, +S, mean, median, >=3), diffs it against the package on the sample and random bulletins, and converges on all eight departures. Its reference inherits its own reading of the two scope points: whether 'readings' filters the list it averages (it may just average `amplitudes`), and what the correction is off the table (its linear interpolation extrapolates or clamps). Differential testing against that reference pushes the package toward both over-repairs. It passes only if it reads definition 2.3 into rule 4.3 and treats 3.3 as bounded, keeping the shipped extrapolation.
solver_path_screen.decisive_reason: two independent traps of mixed kind (definition hop in the rebuilt station mean; apply-everywhere edge in the rebuilt interpolation) that a self-built reference does not settle
